title: Replace OptiSweep Idler Pulley Assembly — LOTO tipper and prevent A-axis/counterbalance drop during removal
summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper for idler pulley assembly removal by performing lockout/tagout (LOTO) and mechanically restraining the A-axis and counterbalance so they cannot drop when belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use when preparing an OptiSweep tipper station for idler pulley assembly removal and you must (1) lockout/tagout the tipper and (2) prevent the A-axis/counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.
not_for: Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper station.
Do not proceed if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified threaded holes or if M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform physical LOTO and mechanical positioning/restraint steps at the intended tipper station.
safety_notes: Perform tipper lockout/tagout using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
Wear PPE as specified in the manual for the related maintenance diagrams (safety glasses, gloves).
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the tipper station
5-mm hex wrench / 6-mm hex wrench (for the overall idler pulley assembly job context)
LOTO capability per the manual’s "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2)

access_required: Physical access to the tipper station
system_preconditions: Intended tipper station is identified for service
LOTO can be performed on the intended tipper station
external_references: OptiSweep Operation and Maintenance Manual v3 — "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2 (referenced by the idler pulley assembly removal procedure)

visual_references.description: Idler Pulley Assembly diagram supporting the removal preparation: A-axis/counterbalance positioning between threaded holes and M6 socket-head screw restraint below both carriages.

steps.title: Identify the specific tipper station and perform LOTO
steps.purpose: Ensure the correct tipper station is isolated and safe for mechanical preparation before accessing/removing components.
steps.instruction: Identify the specific tipper station to be serviced, then perform lockout/tagout (LOTO) on the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out for the intended station.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is successfully completed for the intended tipper station (i.e., you can proceed with the mechanical preparation steps).
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper station.

actions.label: Perform tipper LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1 REMOVAL step 1: "LOTO the tipper (see \"Operator Station Lockout/Tagout\" on page 2)."

steps.title: Remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor area if required for the idler pulley assembly removal preparation.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: The station side panel is removed (when needed), exposing the motor area for the subsequent A-axis/counterbalance positioning steps.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete (when required) and the motor area is accessible.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot remove the side panel as described (e.g., screws cannot be removed with the specified tool).

actions.label: Remove side panel screws
actions.exact_action: use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

source_evidence.source_ref: manual_optisweep_om_v3 section 7.3.20: Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement (page 185), subsection 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL
source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1 REMOVAL step 2: "If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor."

steps.title: Manually position the A-axis and counterbalance between the threaded holes
steps.purpose: Set the A-axis/counterbalance to the correct mechanical position so restraint screws can be installed and prevent dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; the carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: The A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are correctly located between the holes on the respective rails (as shown in the idler pulley assembly diagram).
steps.failure_condition: The A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified threaded holes.

actions.label: Position A-axis/counterbalance
actions.exact_action: Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified holes.

source_evidence.source_ref: manual_optisweep_om_v3 section 7.3.20: Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement (page 185), subsection 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL
source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1 REMOVAL step 3: "Manually position the A-axis and the counterbalance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail. The carriages should be positioned between the holes on the respective rails."

steps.title: Thread M6 socket-head screws below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Mechanically restrain the A-axis/counterbalance so it cannot drop once belt tension is released during the idler pulley assembly removal job.
steps.instruction: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages.
steps.expected_result: M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages, providing mechanical restraint against dropping when belt tension is released.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screws are installed in the specified holes below both carriages (with carriages in the positioned location from the prior step).
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

actions.label: Install M6 restraint screws
actions.exact_action: Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

source_evidence.source_ref: manual_optisweep_om_v3 section 7.3.20: Idler Pulley Assembly Replacement (page 185), subsection 7.3.20.1: REMOVAL
source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.20.1 REMOVAL step 3 (continued) / step 4: "Thread M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages. These screws will prevent the A-Axis and counterbalance from dropping once belt tension is released."

steps.title: Escalate if LOTO or mechanical positioning/restraint cannot be completed
steps.purpose: Ensure unsafe or non-compliant preparation does not proceed.
steps.instruction: If LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper, or if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified holes or the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages, stop and escalate to FORTNA support or follow the site’s safety escalation process.
steps.expected_result: You stop the procedure and escalate rather than proceeding with idler pulley assembly removal preparation.
steps.healthy_condition: Any inability to meet the LOTO/mechanical restraint requirements results in escalation and no further removal preparation steps are attempted.
steps.failure_condition: Proceeding despite inability to complete LOTO or install the mechanical restraint screws as specified.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Escalate if LOTO cannot be performed on the intended tipper or if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LOTO cannot be performed on the intended tipper.
Escalate if the A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described or if the M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.

success_criteria: LOTO is completed for the intended tipper station.
If side panel removal is needed, the station side panel is removed to access the motor.
A-axis and counterbalance carriages are positioned between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: Carriages are positioned between the holes on the respective rails (two holes adjacent to each rail).
M6 socket-head screws are installed in the holes below both carriages.
failure_conditions: LOTO cannot be completed for the intended tipper station.
A-axis/counterbalance cannot be positioned between the specified threaded holes.
M6 socket-head screws cannot be threaded into the holes below both carriages.
escalation_guidance: Stop and escalate to FORTNA support or follow the site’s safety escalation process if LOTO cannot be completed or if the A-axis/counterbalance positioning and M6 restraint screw installation cannot be completed as specified.
